newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia sets April date for key local polls.
newsitem.headline: Croatia sets April date for key local polls.

text.p: Croatia announced on Wednesday that elections for municipal councils, including a Serb-held enclave due to return to central government rule, had been postponed for a month because of problems registering voters.

The Zagreb government announced that the elections for local councils and for the upper house of parliament, which had been expected to fall on March 16, would now be held on April 13 following the intervention of the U.N. team administering the region.
The head of the U.N. Transitional Administration (UNTAES), Jacques Klein, asked President Franjo Tudjman on Monday to reschedule the poll in order to enable full participation by local Serbs.
Some 100,000 Serbs currently living in the area are eligible to vote in the polls if they can prove that they lived in Croatia in 1991.
Serbs took control of the region in 1991, after rebelling against Croatia's bid for independence from former communist Yugoslavia.
Eastern Slavonia, which borders Serbia, is supposed to come back under Zagreb's full rule after the elections, and U.N. peace troops are due to withdraw by July 15.
In the rest of the country, the poll is regarded as the most serious test for Tudjman's ruling Croatian Democratic Union (HDZ) since the end of the war.
The party, which led the nation successfully through a bloody war for independence, has failed to meet the peace-time expectations of a large portion of the public.

An extensive country-wide poll in the independent weekly Nacional published on Tuesday showed that if the elections for the House of Counties -- the upper house -- were held today, HDZ would come second behind a centrist coalition.
The Social Liberals and the Croatian Peasant Party would jointly win 33 of the 68 seats in the house, with the HDZ getting only 25, the poll showed.
An independent Rijeka daily Novi List said the HDZ is likely to base its campaign on the continuing popularity of Tudjman, who is reported to be ill with incurable stomach cancer.

Tudjman announced recently that he planned to stand again in presidential elections this summer, but according to analysts his position would be greatly weakened if the HDZ did badly in the forthcoming elections.
